A_target.statement:
Let $\struct {P, \le}$ be a finite [[Definition:Partially Ordered Set|partially ordered set]].
Then the minimum number of [[Definition:Chain (Order Theory)|chains]] covering $P$ equals the maximum size of an [[Definition:Antichain|antichain]].

B_source.statement: In a finite [[Definition:Bipartite Graph|bipartite graph]], the maximum size of a [[Definition:Matching (Graph Theory)|matching]] equals the minimum size of a [[Definition:Vertex Cover|vertex cover]].

substitutions.the bipartite graph: two copies P' and P'' of P, with x' joined to y'' when x < y
substitutions.matching edges: links between consecutive elements of a chain

object_map.reformulation: Encode chain covers as matchings in the comparability bipartite graph.

validity_conditions: A matching of size m corresponds to a cover by |P| - m chains, as each edge merges two chains.
Uncovered elements in both copies form an antichain, since any comparable pair would give an uncovered edge.
proof_plan: Let $G$ have parts $P' = \set {x'}$ and $P'' = \set {y''}$, with $x' y''$ an edge {{iff}} $x < y$.

A matching $M$ links each $x$ to at most one successor and each $y$ to at most one predecessor, so it splits $P$ into $\card P - \card M$ chains, and conversely.
Hence the minimum number of chains is $\card P - \nu$, where $\nu$ is the maximum matching size.
